from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup data
        title_text = "The Hook: Same World, Different Languages"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- One location can be described by different landmarks.",
            "- Similarly, vectors are described using different bases.",
            "- A vector is a fixed point in space.",
            "- Coordinates depend entirely on the chosen grid."
        ]
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_MOUSE = "#FFD700"  # Yellow
        COLOR_LUNA = "#00FFFF"   # Cyan
        COLOR_ROBO = "#FF00FF"   # Magenta
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first point
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_MOUSE))
        
        # Toy Mouse (the fixed point)
        mouse = Dot(color=COLOR_MOUSE, radius=0.15)
        # Centering the mouse in the middle of the 6x6 grid area
        self.place_in_area(mouse, "C3", "D4")
        
        mouse_label = Text("Toy Mouse", font_size=16, color=COLOR_MOUSE)
        # Position label relative to mouse but anchored to grid
        mouse_label.next_to(mouse, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(mouse), Write(mouse_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Shift focus to Luna's perspective
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_LUNA)
        )
        
        # Luna's grid
        luna_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_LUNA, "stroke_opacity": 0.3},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": COLOR_LUNA, "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        self.place_in_area(luna_grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Window Landmark (one of Luna's landmarks)
        window_icon = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=0.4, color=COLOR_LUNA),
            Line(start=[-0.2, 0, 0], end=[0.2, 0, 0], color=COLOR_LUNA),
            Line(start=[0, -0.2, 0], end=[0, 0.2, 0], color=COLOR_LUNA)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(window_icon, "C6") # On the x-axis for Luna
        window_label = Text("Window", font_size=14, color=COLOR_LUNA).next_to(window_icon, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        luna_stuff = VGroup(luna_grid, window_icon, window_label)
        self.play(FadeIn(luna_stuff))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Emphasize that the mouse (vector) doesn't move
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_MOUSE)
        )
        
        self.play(mouse.animate.scale(1.5), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(mouse.animate.scale(1/1.5), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Transition to Robo-1's perspective
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_ROBO)
        )
        
        # Robo-1's grid (rotated relative to Luna's)
        robo_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_ROBO, "stroke_opacity": 0.3},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": COLOR_ROBO, "stroke_width": 2}
        ).rotate(45 * DEGREES)
        self.place_in_area(robo_grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Charging Station Landmark (Robo-1's landmark)
        charger_icon = VGroup(
            Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.3, color=COLOR_ROBO),
            Triangle(color=COLOR_ROBO).scale(0.1).rotate(180*DEGREES).move_to([0, 0.1, 0])
        )
        # Position at A3 relative to the right side area
        self.place_at_grid(charger_icon, "A3")
        charger_label = Text("Charger", font_size=14, color=COLOR_ROBO).next_to(charger_icon, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        robo_stuff = VGroup(robo_grid, charger_icon, charger_label)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(luna_stuff, robo_stuff),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "Prerequisite Review: What is a Basis?"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Standard unit vectors define our common grid.",
            "A basis acts as a set of measuring rulers.",
            "Every vector is a combination of these basis vectors."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Color definitions
        COLOR_I = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_J = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_GRID = "#444444"
        COLOR_VECTOR = "#FFFFFF" # White

        # Origin point at D2 (standard origin for this section)
        origin_coords = self.grid["D2"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_I), run_time=0.5)
        
        grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": COLOR_GRID,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.6
            },
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_color": COLOR_GRID}
        )
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A1", "F6")

        # Basis vectors relative to origin
        i_vec = Arrow(
            start=origin_coords,
            end=origin_coords + np.array([1, 0, 0]),
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_I,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        j_vec = Arrow(
            start=origin_coords,
            end=origin_coords + np.array([0, 1, 0]),
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_J,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        i_label = Text("i", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_I, font_size=24)
        j_label = Text("j", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_J, font_size=24)
        
        i_label.next_to(i_vec, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_label.next_to(j_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(grid), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(i_vec), 
            GrowArrow(j_vec), 
            Write(i_label), 
            Write(j_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_J), run_time=0.5)
        
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                Flash(i_vec, color=COLOR_I, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=1.1),
                Flash(j_vec, color=COLOR_J, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=1.1),
                i_vec.animate.set_stroke_width(8),
                j_vec.animate.set_stroke_width(8),
                run_time=0.5
            )
            self.play(
                i_vec.animate.set_stroke_width(4),
                j_vec.animate.set_stroke_width(4),
                run_time=0.5
            )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_VECTOR), run_time=0.5)
        
        v_target_rel = np.array([3, 2, 0])
        v_target_abs = origin_coords + v_target_rel
        
        main_vector = Arrow(
            start=origin_coords,
            end=v_target_abs,
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_VECTOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        # Replacing MathTex with Text
        v_label = Text("v = 3i + 2j", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_VECTOR, font_size=24)
        v_label.next_to(main_vector.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Component lines to show projection
        i_comp_line = Line(
            start=origin_coords,
            end=origin_coords + np.array([3, 0, 0]),
            color=COLOR_I,
            stroke_width=2
        ).set_opacity(0.5)
        
        j_comp_line = Line(
            start=origin_coords + np.array([3, 0, 0]),
            end=v_target_abs,
            color=COLOR_J,
            stroke_width=2
        ).set_opacity(0.5)

        self.play(Create(i_comp_line), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Create(j_comp_line), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(main_vector), 
            Write(v_label), 
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.wait(2)

                y_coord = 2.2 - i * 1.0

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout (Title and Lecture Content)
        title_text = "The Art of Perspective: Change of Basis"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Understanding Basis Vectors",
            "- Defining the Transformation",
            "- Mapping Standard to New Basis",
            "- Geometric Interpretation"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # 2. Define a Coordinate System on the Right Side
        # Center the visual area on the grid around "C3"
        visual_center = self.grid["C3"]
        
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": BLUE_D,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.5
            }
        ).move_to(visual_center)
        
        basis_i = Arrow(visual_center, visual_center + RIGHT, buff=0, color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
        basis_j = Arrow(visual_center, visual_center + UP, buff=0, color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        label_i = Text("i", color=GREEN).scale(0.6).next_to(basis_i, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_j = Text("j", color=RED).scale(0.6).next_to(basis_j, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # 3. Animations
        self.play(Write(self.title))
        self.play(Write(self.lecture), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(GrowArrow(basis_i), GrowArrow(basis_j))
        self.play(Write(label_i), Write(label_j))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Show Change of Basis (Shear Transformation)
        # Transformation matrix: [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        
        # Target vectors
        new_i_end = visual_center + RIGHT
        new_j_end = visual_center + RIGHT + UP
        
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            basis_i.animate.put_start_and_end_on(visual_center, new_i_end),
            basis_j.animate.put_start_and_end_on(visual_center, new_j_end),
            label_i.animate.next_to(new_i_end, DOWN, buff=0.1),
            label_j.animate.next_to(new_j_end, UP, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x_coord = 1.5 + j * 1.0

        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize title and lecture lines
        title_text = "Summary and Visual Wrap-up"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are absolute, but their coordinates are relative.",
            "The transition matrix P connects different coordinate perspectives.",
            "This concept is fundamental to modern science and technology."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Vectors are absolute, but their coordinates are relative.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Standard Grid (#444444)
        std_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#444444", "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#444444"}
        )
        self.place_in_area(std_grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # White vector arrow (#FFFFFF)
        grid_center = std_grid.get_center()
        # Arrow from (0,0) to (2,1) in plane units
        vec = Arrow(
            grid_center,
            grid_center + np.array([1.6, 0.8, 0]), 
            buff=0,
            color="#FFFFFF",
            stroke_width=6
        )

        self.play(Create(std_grid), GrowArrow(vec), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The transition matrix P connects different coordinate perspectives.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create target tilted purple grid (#AA00FF)
        tilted_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#AA00FF", "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#AA00FF"}
        )
        self.place_in_area(tilted_grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Apply transformation to the tilted grid
        matrix = [[1.2, -0.5], [0.3, 1.0]]
        tilted_grid.apply_matrix(matrix)

        # Morph the grid while keeping the vector still
        self.play(
            Transform(std_grid, tilted_grid),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # This concept is fundamental to modern science and technology.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Final formula [v]_S = P [v]_B - Replaced MathTex with Text due to missing LaTeX environment
        formula = Text("[v]_S = P [v]_B", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "C2", "D5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Black background for formula for legibility over the grid
        bg_rect = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0.8, buff=0.2)

        self.play(FadeIn(bg_rect), FadeIn(formula))
        # Scale it up for emphasis
        self.play(formula.animate.scale(1.3), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Fade to black
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(self.title, self.lecture, std_grid, vec, bg_rect, formula)))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Art of Perspective: Understanding Change of Basis
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM or advanced high school linear algebra students

sections.title: The Hook: Same World, Different Languages
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'perspective.' Just as two people might describe the same location using different landmarks, mathematicians describe the same vector using different 'bases.' Establish that a vector is an absolute point in space, but its coordinates depend entirely on the grid we choose.
sections.example: Imagine a cat (Luna) and a robot (Robo-1). Luna sees 'forward' as the direction of the sunny window, while Robo-1 sees 'forward' as the direction of its charging station. They are looking at the same toy mouse, but they describe its position with different numbers.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: What is a Basis?
sections.content: Briefly refresh the concepts of basis vectors (i and j) and linear combinations. Visualize the standard Cartesian grid. Explain that a basis is simply a set of 'unit rulers' used to measure space. To be a basis, the vectors must be linearly independent and span the space.
sections.example: Show the standard grid with unit vectors e1=(1,0) and e2=(0,1). An arrow pointing to (3,2) is just 3 steps of e1 and 2 steps of e2.

sections.title: The Core Problem: The Tilted Grid
sections.content: Introduce a second, 'tilted' coordinate system (Basis B). Show visually how the same vector (the toy mouse) stays fixed in space while the background grid rotates or stretches. The goal is to find a mathematical 'translator' between the Standard Basis (S) and the Tilted Basis (B).
sections.example: Overlay a standard square grid with a diagonal, diamond-shaped grid. Point out that the vector (1,1) in the square grid might look like (1,0) in the diamond grid.

sections.title: The Solution: The Transition Matrix
sections.content: Introduce the Change of Basis Matrix (P). Explain that the columns of this matrix are simply the basis vectors of the 'new' system written in the language of the 'old' system. This matrix acts as a bridge: [v]_old = P * [v]_new.
sections.example: If Basis B's 'forward' vector is (1,1) in standard terms and its 'sideways' vector is (-1,1), we put these into the columns of matrix P. Now, any coordinate in B's world can be instantly converted to our standard world.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Calculation: Converting Coordinates
sections.content: Demonstrate the 'Inverse' operation. If we know where the mouse is in our world, how do we tell the Robot where it is in its world? Use the inverse of the Transition Matrix (P^-1). Show the algebraic flow clearly.
sections.example: The mouse is at (2,4) in our grid. By multiplying (2,4) by P-inverse, we calculate that for the Robot, the mouse is at (3,1) relative to its own sensors.

sections.title: Summary and Visual Wrap-up
sections.content: Recap the three key components: The fixed Vector, the two different Bases, and the Transition Matrix that connects them. Emphasize that Change of Basis is the foundation for computer graphics, GPS navigation, and quantum mechanics.
sections.example: Animation showing the grid morphing from square to tilted while the vector remains a solid, unmoving arrow, concluding with the formula: [v]_S = P [v]_B.

storyboard.title: The Hook: Same World, Different Languages
lecture_lines: One point can be described by different landmarks.
A vector exists as a fixed point in space.
But its coordinates depend on the chosen grid.
animations: Show a yellow toy mouse [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mouse.svg] (#FFD700) as a fixed point in the center of the screen.
Fade in Luna's cyan coordinate grid (#00FFFF) centered on the mouse [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mouse.svg], with one axis pointing to a window icon.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: What is a Basis?
lecture_lines: Standard unit vectors define our common grid.
A basis acts as a set of measuring rulers.
Every vector is a combination of these basis vectors.
animations: Draw a standard gray grid (#444444) and unit vectors i=(1,0) in green (#00FF00) and j=(0,1) in red (#FF0000).
Create a white vector (#FFFFFF) starting at origin and ending at (3,2), showing it as a combination of 3i and 2j.
Flash the i and j vectors twice to highlight them as the standard basis for this grid.

storyboard.title: The Core Problem: The Tilted Grid
lecture_lines: Start with a vector in the standard coordinate system.
Now, introduce a new, tilted grid called Basis B.
Basis B uses its own unique set of unit vectors.
The vector remains fixed as we swap underlying grids.
Notice how its coordinates change in this new perspective.
animations: Display a fixed white vector v=(2,2) (#FFFFFF) on a standard dark gray grid (#444444).
Slowly fade in a tilted purple grid (#AA00FF) that is rotated and scaled relative to the standard grid.
Show basis vectors b1=(1,1) in green (#00FF00) and b2=(-1,1) in red (#FF0000) for the tilted grid.
Keep the white vector v completely stationary while the underlying grids toggle between standard and tilted.
Label the vector v as (2,2) in the standard basis and (2,0) in the tilted basis.

storyboard.title: The Solution: The Transition Matrix
lecture_lines: Describe the new basis using our standard coordinates.
Place these vectors into the columns of matrix P.
This formula defines the conversion between coordinate systems.
Matrix P transforms new coordinates back to old ones.
The columns are the new basis in old terms.
animations: Display vectors b1=(1,1) and b2=(-1,1) clearly on the standard grid to show their standard coordinates.
Construct Matrix P (#FFFF00) by placing b1 and b2 as its columns: [[1, -1], [1, 1]].
Write the formula [v]_S = P * [v]_B in a bright cyan color (#00FFFF) at the top of the screen.
Animate the multiplication: take vector [2,0] in Basis B and show it transforming into [2,2] in Standard Basis.
Highlight the columns of Matrix P with flashing boxes to emphasize they are the 'new' basis vectors.

storyboard.title: Step-by-Step Calculation: Converting Coordinates
lecture_lines: Use the inverse matrix to convert coordinates back.
This tells us the vector's position in the new basis.
Calculating this allows us to see through the robot's eyes.
animations: Display the formula [v]_B = P-inverse * [v]_S in orange (#FFA500) to show the reverse conversion.
Show the symbolic calculation of P-inverse and its multiplication with a standard vector (2,4) (#FFFFFF).
Update the visual to show the vector (2,4) being located at (3,1) within the tilted grid coordinate system.

storyboard.title: Summary and Visual Wrap-up
lecture_lines: Vectors are absolute, but their coordinates are relative.
The transition matrix P connects different coordinate perspectives.
This concept is fundamental to modern science and technology.
animations: Animate the grid smoothly morphing from the standard square grid (#444444) to the tilted purple grid (#AA00FF).
Ensure the white vector arrow (#FFFFFF) remains perfectly still during the entire grid transformation.
Fade in the final formula [v]_S = P [v]_B in the center, then scale it up for emphasis before fading to black.
